note: Durations and absolute paths are normalised so a re-record diffs only on real format changes. The JUnit XML additionally has its hostname, timestamp and per-test time normalised: Gradle writes the recording machine's hostname into every testsuite element.

fixtures.name: gradle_rerun_unknown_option
fixtures.description: Gradle older than 7.6 asked for a task's --rerun, which build_and_test passes to every test task so that an UP-TO-DATE task cannot leave an older run's reports to be read as this run's (N6). The option arrived in 7.6; before it Gradle stops in the '* What went wrong:' block with 'Problem configuring task ... from command line.' and '> Unknown command-line option '--rerun'.', exit 1. Recorded so the skill can say why, instead of a bare Build: FAILED.

fixtures.name: gradle_properties_project_dir
fixtures.description: The module-directory question build_and_test asks for --module, against a settings script with no projectDir override. Even under -q Gradle prints a dashed `Project ':app'` banner first, then exactly one `projectDir: <absolute path>` line -- the conventional app/ directory.

fixtures.name: gradle_properties_project_dir_remapped
fixtures.setup: run in a temporary copy of the scaffold; appended to settings.gradle: "project(':app').projectDir = file('mobile')\n"; created: mobile
fixtures.description: The same question on a copy of the scaffold whose settings.gradle ends with `project(':app').projectDir = file('mobile')` and has a mobile/ directory. Gradle answers mobile/: the directory the test task writes its reports under, and so the one cleanup and collection must use.

fixtures.name: gradle_properties_unknown_project
fixtures.description: The question asked about a module the build does not have: exit 1 and a '* What went wrong:' block, no projectDir line. The wording differs by version -- 8.13 says "Cannot locate tasks that match ':nope:properties' as project 'nope' not found in root project ...", 7.5.1 says "Project 'nope' not found in root project ...".

fixtures.name: gradle_properties_no_such_property
fixtures.description: A property filter that matches nothing still exits 0, prints the banner and `noSuchPropertyAnywhere: null` -- an honest successful answer with no projectDir line in it, which the builder must refuse rather than fall back to a guessed directory.
